authorization: etymologise remaining Indo-Aryan surveys. do not rebuild. work autonomously and do what you can, you have 8 hours, i will review once your time is done.

proposals.evidence: Platts explicitly labels ćāqū “clasp-knife, penknife” Persian; the existing Hindi cākū attestation in the Kannauji survey supplies an attested regional donor with q adapted to k. The selected c/ts, aspiration, gemination and vowel variants preserve the whole knife word. This follows the previous review’s provisional Hindi/Urdu transmission policy, leaving local Gujarati, Pashto or other intermediaries unresolved; mixed slash responses and metathesized kācū are excluded.

proposals.evidence: Platts explicitly records Persian garm and vernacular garam “hot, warm”; the linked Hindi garam survey attestation is the existing regional donor. These whole adjectives are linked as regional loans with unresolved local transmission, not as direct descendants of cognate Sanskrit gharma. Responses in -i “heat” and combinations with the inherited tatta adjective are excluded.
